PullRequest.Title: agentHost: enrich turn telemetry with interactions and steering origins
PullRequest.Body:

## What and why

Make Copilot runtime interactions joinable to AH lifecycle data on existing telemetry events, and retain the original request when confirmed steering splits its execution into several AH turns.

The distinction matters near completion: AH can promote a message as steering while the runtime processes it as a new idle-run request. This change records that disagreement rather than automatically charging the new request to the old one.

| Existing event | Added information |
| --- | --- |
| `agentHost.turnCompleted` | SDK session, bounded JSON array of observed interaction IDs with a truncation flag, known original turn, and host steering predecessor |
| `copilotSdk/response.success` / `response.error` | Known original turn and host steering predecessor, only with exact ownership |
| `agentHost.modelCallTurnCorrelated` | Known original turn and host steering predecessor, including late mappings |

Retains one new event, `agentHost.turnSteered`, emitted when the promoted message's SDK echo establishes its delivery. It carries `steeredFromTurn`, runtime delivery and attribution status independently of eventual completion. The earlier separate `turnInteractionCorrelated` event is removed.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10773. This covers steering and observed interaction associations, not complete cross-chat originating-trigger attribution.

## Attribution rules

- Runtime `steering` delivery sharing an observed predecessor interaction retains the original turn, including across repeated steering.
- Runtime `idle` or `queued` delivery starts its own origin, even if AH promoted it as steering.
- Changed interactions on steering delivery and missing evidence leave the original turn unresolved. `steeredFromTurn` describes the host's predecessor, not proof of runtime continuity.
- Independent requests keep their own origin. Execution-turn IDs and UI routing are not merged or changed.

The snapshots retain many-to-many associations rather than selecting one interaction. History is bounded and cleared on disposal; there is no disk persistence or extension of active execution-routing map lifetimes. Completion snapshots contain evidence known at emission; the existing response/call bridge remains necessary for late evidence. Missing completions and unowned calls still produce coverage gaps.

## Manual verification

Exercised Code OSS on Windows with Copilot Agent Host and trace logging. The logs showed:

1. A genuine steering echo reported `runtimeDelivery=steering`, `attributionStatus=confirmed`, and retained the original request across response, call-bridge and completion events.
2. The completion-boundary race reproduced: AH promoted the next message as steering, but the SDK reported `runtimeDelivery=idle`. It was recorded as `newRequest`; all three existing event families carried that new turn's own origin instead of the predecessor's.
3. A subsequent ordinary submission retained its own origin. No `turnInteractionCorrelated` events were emitted.

To reproduce, start a request that remains active, steer it, then send another message near completion and another after idle. Compare `turnSteered.runtimeDelivery` and `attributionStatus` with the enriched response/bridge/completion rows in `agentHostTelemetry.log`. The boundary race is timing-dependent; a rendered answer alone is not evidence that the SDK is idle.

This verifies local emission and behavior, not backend ingestion or complete descendant attribution. The original host/runtime classification disagreement remains observable; this PR does not change how the UI or runtime executes messages.

## Follow-up: submission intent versus runtime delivery

Tracked separately in [microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10893](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/10893). AH's legacy `receivedSteering` / `startedWithSteering` flags are set from accepted pending-message intent and host promotion. They do not establish that the runtime consumed the input inside the preceding interaction. SDK `mode: 'immediate'` is also a submission option; the `user.message.delivery` echo supplies the actual delivery outcome.

For the reproduced `idle` case, this PR already prevents incorrect inheritance of the predecessor's original-turn ID. Remaining inaccuracy is in interpreting the legacy steering classification: neither those flags, `steeredFromTurn`, nor the presence of a `turnSteered` event alone proves runtime continuity. Use `attributionStatus=confirmed` for confirmed continuity and retain unknown/mismatched cases as coverage gaps.

Aligning host lifecycle classification with provider confirmation is left to that follow-up because it must preserve idle-before-echo promotion, queue cleanup, cancellation/withdrawal and exactly-once message execution. No behavior changes for those paths are included here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a Copilot session, accumulate ordinary and child-turn correlation history, then cancel or dispose it.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session construction adds an empty LRU; starting a root turn adds an empty Set and scalar state synchronously. Recording interaction evidence performs in-memory lookups and bounded insertion, without starting provider, database, filesystem, or network work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live SDK sessions, observed execution-turn IDs, and distinct interactions per turn. Each session retains at most 1,000 correlation entries and 64 interaction IDs per entry; unresolved steering can additionally retain a predecessor snapshot of at most 64 IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: State mutations are synchronous on the host JavaScript thread. The diff adds no task fan-out, timers, subprocesses, or background initialization. Existing active execution-routing Sets are still cleared with CopilotTurn disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The LRU starts empty, creates entries on startTurn or an exact response association, deduplicates IDs with Set.has, marks overflow without retaining additional IDs, and evicts old turns. Missing reads do not trigger recovery I/O. Registered disposal clears the LRU. Predecessor contexts contain scalar IDs and flat arrays, not recursive links to turn objects.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the complete new correlation implementation, LRU trimming, constructor disposal registration, CopilotTurn disposal, and session super.dispose path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual live-session counts and interaction counts are unmeasured; the retained history is explicitly bounded rather than proportional to the entire session lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable retention, eager-initialization, or cleanup regression established. The added bounded analytical history does not extend the lifetime of active execution-routing objects.

Scenarios.Scenario: Process an ordinary SDK user-message echo or assistant turn-start event.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new _recordTurnInteraction helper adds one bounded correlation insertion beside the existing active-turn Set insertion. Existing asynchronous persistence and repository telemetry remain at their prior call sites and are not awaited by the new helper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the turn's SDK event boundary and optional completion-reference metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One database-reference scope per processed root user-message echo. setTurnEventId issues an INSERT OR IGNORE and conditional UPDATE; completion-reference metadata is written only when references exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same database operations and Promise.all launch existed before the diff. The new interaction helper neither invokes nor multiplies them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already launched asynchronously without awaiting database completion before returning from the message handler.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Root user-message echoes and root assistant.turn_start events, not streaming message deltas or every rendered token. Duplicate interaction IDs do not enlarge the analytical Set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The added work is synchronous in the existing SDK event handlers. Existing user-message persistence submits two promises through Promise.all, but database mutations share the database mutation sequencer; the diff does not increase that concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing turn entries are reused; duplicate interaction IDs return immediately. Missing analytical entries are created locally without replaying history or resolving provider state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced both replaced Set.add sites, the new helper, user-message filtering, persistence helper, optional metadata write, and database sequencing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK event frequency and persistence latency vary, but neither persistence cardinality nor scheduling changes in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added in-memory work is bounded and occurs at interaction boundaries rather than on the high-frequency streaming path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete, fail, or cancel a tracked turn and enrich agentHost.turnCompleted.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tracker samples terminal timing, performs a synchronous exact-chat lookup and bounded snapshot, then enriches the existing completion event. JSON serialization handles at most 64 retained interaction IDs. No provider fetch or telemetry-delivery wait is added before turn completion proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the bounded interaction-ID snapshot into the existing completion event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional JSON array serialization per enriched completion, with no more than 64 IDs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Completion telemetry did not serialize this interaction list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small bounded synchronous work in terminal telemetry preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pass the existing telemetry row to the trace logger for local telemetry logging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing one completion row per tracked terminal turn; only its bounded payload is enriched.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion event already passed through this logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new filesystem read or awaited log flush is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Track the completion row in the existing collector and send collector-managed telemetry payloads asynchronously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged completion-event count. HTTP requests are collector-managed rather than one new request per interaction ID; exact batching remains SDK-controlled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The completion row already used this collector and transport; the diff adds fields, not another event or delivery wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Collector initialization is shared and asynchronous; HTTP delivery is not awaited by turn completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One enrichment per tracked terminal turn; duplicate terminal actions return before collection. Work scales with retained IDs for that turn, capped at 64, not with all historical turns or model-call records.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Snapshotting and event preparation run synchronously. Existing telemetry appenders receive the same single completion event; the collector's asynchronous transport is not awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm reads copy the cached bounded Set; absent or evicted evidence returns undefined without I/O or reconstruction. Chat and SDK-session lookup use maps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced terminal-action deduplication, getTurnInteraction through map-based chat lookup, bounded snapshot construction, reporter serialization, telemetry delegation, appenders, and asynchronous transport.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured serialization or log-write timings. Normal identifier lengths and the enforced count cap provide no evidence of a concrete user-visible slowdown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added serialization is bounded before allocation and does not fan out into per-ID events or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Forward response telemetry and publish exact or late model-call ownership bridges.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK telemetry routing is launched without awaiting it in the runtime notification callback. Cached ownership forwards immediately; missing ownership can use the existing 100 ms correlation wait. The diff adds local interaction recording and a bounded snapshot only after exact ownership is available; it adds no await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the existing response row and existing model-call correlation bridge through the standard telemetry collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same response-row count and same nonduplicate/conflict bridge publication rules as before. No new interaction-mapping event or per-interaction transport request is emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both event families and the correlation wait already existed; only bounded cached lineage fields are added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous collector delivery remains off the request-execution critical path. The pre-existing correlation wait is not lengthened.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response.success/error rows and nonduplicate model-call mappings, including child calls. Each exact response records at most one observed ID; lineage reads copy at most 64 IDs. Bridge event deduplication remains keyed by model-call ID within its bounded history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Different model-call IDs may wait concurrently as before, while waiters for the same ID share the pending mapping. Added map/Set operations are synchronous and launch no parallel work. Duplicate mapping status still suppresses bridge publication.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm model-call mappings are consumed directly. Cold waits share a DeferredPromise per call ID and remain timeout-bounded; already-forwarded and expired responses do not initiate analytical recovery. Late bridges use current cached lineage without extending the wait. Compaction retains its existing separate correlation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced runtime fire-and-forget routing, response ownership branches, the complete ModelCallTurnCorrelation cache/wait implementation, root and remapped child callers, duplicate suppression, and forwarder publication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Concurrent model-call counts and telemetry transport latency are unmeasured, but the diff changes neither wait duration, event multiplicity, nor boundary concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable fan-out, missing-coalescing, or latency regression. Snapshot copying is capped and no richer metadata causes additional downstream provider work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Promote steering during execution or at the idle-before-echo boundary, including repeated steering.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Promotion captures at most 64 predecessor interaction IDs before disposing the previous execution turn. Echo resolution performs a bounded membership check and emits one small steering event. The existing execution-turn completion/start actions and runtime message delivery remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the new agentHost.turnSteered row via the existing standard telemetry service and collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one small event for each prepared steering state that receives a resolving matched echo, not one event per observed interaction or predecessor in the chain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No turnSteered row was emitted. Completion and model-call telemetry already ran for promoted execution turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous telemetry preparation is small and fixed-field; asynchronous collector delivery is not awaited by the SDK handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Log the additional small steering telemetry row through the existing trace logger when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional row per resolved steering state, independent of the number of retained interactions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no steering-specific row, although the surrounding execution telemetry already used this logger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new read or awaited flush; existing logger ownership and scheduling remain unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Promoted steering messages and their matched SDK echoes. Repeated steering stores the original-turn scalar and immediate predecessor snapshot rather than walking or retaining the full chain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promotion and echo resolution are synchronous in existing event handlers. There is no new concurrent SDK send, correlation wait, database persistence, or provider lookup. Existing execution-turn routing ownership is not extended.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Predecessor context is captured from the bounded cache or carried across the existing idle race. Resolving steering clears its pending context before publishing; repeated resolution cannot emit another event from that state. Unresolved contexts remain limited by LRU eviction and session disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced promotion, ordinary echo resolution, idle-before-echo predecessor capture, context clearing, tests for repeated steering, and existing telemetry transport.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Steering frequency and collector batch composition are unmeasured. There is no evidence that one fixed-field event per user steering operation causes a material performance problem.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. New event cardinality follows steering operations, not interaction history, and repeated steering introduces no recursive retention or boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 13 changed files and every diff page against base af6eb6cfb3972f0926279459ee0298922ac79854. Investigated bounded correlation retention, snapshot/serialization costs, exact and late response ownership, steering races, disposal, database sequencing, and telemetry transport. No high-confidence actionable performance regressions found, and no concrete performance-regression fix requiring blame provenance was identified. Static analysis only; runtime magnitude was not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
